name: How does a zero-threshold shower differ from a standard walk-in shower conversion?

mainEntity.name: How does a zero-threshold shower differ from a standard walk-in shower conversion?

acceptedAnswer.text: A tub-to-shower conversion replaces an existing high-sided bathtub with a walk-in or roll-in shower. A standard conversion typically installs a low-profile curb that still requires stepping up an inch or two, making it ideal for general aging-in-place. A zero-threshold shower eliminates the curb entirely, creating a flush transition with the bathroom floor. While zero-threshold designs provide seamless wheelchair roll-in access, they require specialized subfloor preparation and sloped drainage to ensure water does not spill into the main bathroom area.
acceptedAnswer.description: Zero-threshold showers sit completely flush with the floor for seamless roll-in access, while standard walk-in showers retain a low step-over curb.
